class_name: 否定-不可能-ワケニハイカナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: This denies permissibility, not ability: the act is perfectly doable, but duty, conscience or circumstances rule it out, which is what separates it from 〜ことができない. Attached to a negated verb it flips into obligation (行かないわけにはいかない, "I have no choice but to go"). It typically describes a human predicament the speaker is inside of, and the fuller written shape is わけにはいかない, with わけにゃ／わけにゃゆかない as spoken contractions.

examples.ruby: 大事[だいじ]な打[う]ち合[あ]わせだから、遅刻[ちこく]するわけにはいかない。
examples.english: It's an important meeting, so I can't afford to turn up late.

examples.ruby: 借[か]りた本[ほん]を汚[よご]したまま返[かえ]すわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I can't very well hand a borrowed book back with a stain still on it.

examples.ruby: ここまで来[き]て、今[いま]さらやめるわけにゃいかない。
examples.english: We've come this far; no way we're quitting now.

patterns.usage_note: わけにはいかない with the conjectural まい fused onto いく, so the refusal is offered as a judgment the hearer is expected to share rather than flatly asserted. It belongs to written narration, speeches and the deliberative inner monologue of older, usually male speakers; ordinary conversation says わけにはいかないだろう instead. まい already carries the negation, so no second negative attaches to いく itself; the preceding verb, however, is freely negative, and 〜ないわけにはいくまい ("one can hardly not …") is the ordinary obligation shape, whose neutral everyday counterpart is 〜ないわけにはいかない.

examples.ruby: これほど世話[せわ]になった相手[あいて]を見捨[みす]てるわけにはいくまい。
examples.english: After all he has done for us, we can hardly abandon him.

examples.ruby: 部下[ぶか]の失態[しったい]なのだから、知[し]らぬ顔[かお]をするわけにはいくまい。
examples.english: It was my subordinate's blunder; I can scarcely pretend not to notice.

examples.ruby: 事[こと]ここに至[いた]っては、真相[しんそう]を伏[ふ]せておくわけにはいくまい。
examples.english: Matters having come to this, it would hardly do to keep the truth hidden.

patterns.usage_note: The negative twin of よう／だろう: with a first-person subject it is negative resolve (二度と行くまい, "I'll never go again"), with a third-person subject negative conjecture ("probably won't"). Godan verbs take the dictionary form; ichidan and する are also found in a shorter shape (見まい, しまい／すまい) beside 見るまい, するまい, and 来る has a contested short form (こまい from the 未然形 beside classical くまい) alongside 来るまい. Everyday speech now prefers ないだろう or ないつもりだ, so まい reads bookish or stiffly formal.

examples.ruby: あんな店[みせ]には二度[にど]と入[はい]るまいと心[こころ]に決[き]めた。
examples.english: I made up my mind never to set foot in that shop again.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]の性格[せいかく]からして、素直[すなお]に認[みと]めるまい。
examples.english: Knowing his temperament, he's unlikely to just admit it.

examples.ruby: この雨[あめ]では、今日[きょう]の試合[しあい]は予定[よてい]どおり始[はじ]まるまい。
examples.english: In this rain today's match surely won't start on schedule.
